title: The Transcript Looked Fine. The Call Wasn't. — Debugging Voice Agents, Arize
talk_summary: Arize PM argues that text transcripts hide real agent failures (latency, interruptions, wrong tool calls) and that you must trace the full session with inputs/outputs, metrics, and evals attached to spans.

takeaways.technique: Attach eval scores to the exact span/trace, not a separate system
takeaways.what_they_do: Run evals live on incoming spans and store scores inline with the trace so you can query/filter failures and correlate them to the exact step that broke.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you also want these evals on the spans themselves because then you start to be able to do really complex querying and filtering across your data

takeaways.technique: Eval-triggered investigation agent that replays failed traces
takeaways.evidence_quote: replaying those failed traces for you against that fixed endpoint, tracing that to validate that the latency actually decreases

takeaways.technique: Truncate tool results to prevent context overload
takeaways.what_they_do: The example SRE-agent fix was that tool results weren't truncated, overloading context and raising latency; adding a truncation algorithm fixed it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we were not truncating our tool results, and so we were passing in way too much information to the agent. Context got overloaded.

takeaways.technique: Agent-as-judge that checks external systems, not just text
takeaways.what_they_do: Move beyond LLM-judge-on-transcript to judges that access tools/third-party systems and hydrate evaluation info, e.g. verifying the agent actually hit the system it was supposed to.
takeaways.evidence_quote: actually accessing tools, accessing third-party systems, and hydrating some of that evaluation information inside of it

takeaways.technique: Unified session trace with per-step metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Stitch all turns/events of a session under one session ID with inputs/outputs, latency, and tool calls inline so you can see who did what when, instead of reading a flat log.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the session ID is essentially what stitches every turn into the timeline, the full call with every websocket event
takeaways.numbers: 2.4 seconds of dead air cited as the hidden latency failure
